painting.title: The Abbey in the Oakwood
painting.pairingNote: A ruin that is more moving for being incomplete, in the hushed, wintry mood of the symphony’s opening.

facts: Schubert wrote two complete movements in 1822 and sketched a third, then stopped. Nobody knows why.
The manuscript sat with a friend for decades. The first performance was on 17 December 1865, 37 years after Schubert’s death.
Both movements are in triple time and at a similar pace, yet they feel like night and day.
Schubert was a songwriter above all. Here the orchestra sings, and the songs keep being interrupted.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a song under threat (I), an uneasy peace (II).

movements.heading: Allegro moderato
movements.summary: A dark phrase in the basses, a restless shimmer, and two of the most beautiful melodies Schubert wrote. The movement is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]], and its drama comes from how brutally the melodies are cut off.

mainIdeas.name: The motto
mainIdeas.description: a low, winding phrase for cellos and basses alone.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a plaintive melody for oboe and clarinet over shimmering violins.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a warm, swaying tune in the cellos. One of the best-known melodies in classical music.

stops.hear: Cellos and basses alone, very quiet, winding downward
stops.happening: The motto. Remember it; it returns later with a vengeance

stops.hear: Nervous, shimmering violins over plucked basses; oboe and clarinet sing together
Horns and bassoons hold a single long note; the mood lifts
stops.happening: A hinge. One held note carries the music into a new key

stops.hear: Cellos sing a gentle, swaying melody; violins take it up
The melody stops in mid-phrase. One bar of silence. Then violent chords
The motto again, sinking lower; then it rises through the whole orchestra to a huge climax with trombones
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] is built almost entirely on the motto. The quiet opening phrase becomes a cry

stops.hear: The shimmer and the oboe melody return
The motto one last time, then stern closing chords

notice: The famous cello tune never appears in the development. Schubert leaves it untouched and works only with the dark motto.
Listen for the silence at ≈ 2:00. It is as important as any note.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: Outwardly serene, with long solo lines for the woodwinds, but the calm is broken by loud, marching episodes.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quiet melody in the violins, introduced by horns and descending plucked basses.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a long, lonely solo for clarinet, later oboe, over softly pulsing strings.

stops.hear: Horns and bassoons, plucked basses stepping down, then a calm violin melody
A sudden loud, striding passage with trombones
stops.happening: The first disturbance. The basses march while the winds call out above

stops.hear: Violins alone hold a thin line of soft notes
A long, searching clarinet solo over gently off-beat strings; the oboe answers in the major
stops.happening: Theme 2. The accompaniment uses [[syncopation|syncopation]], which gives it its floating quality

stops.hear: The clarinet’s melody is seized by the full orchestra, fortissimo

stops.happening: The first half is repeated with the keys changed

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: Violins alone drift into a distant key and back; the music settles
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. A peaceful ending that sounds, for many listeners, like a true conclusion

notice: Both movements follow the same pattern: a song, an interruption, the song again. That shared shape is part of why the two movements feel complete together.

threads.title: Song against force
threads.body: In both movements lyrical melodies are broken off by violent outbursts.

threads.title: Quiet trombones
threads.body: Schubert often uses the trombones softly, as a dark colour, not just for power.

threads.title: Unfinished, yet whole
threads.body: The second movement ends in a calm that feels final.
